# Frontend Design

Use this skill when implementing or reshaping a frontend interface.

## Workflow

1. Identify the product subject, audience, and primary user job.
2. Define a compact visual system before coding:
   - 4-6 named colors with hex values
   - typefaces and roles
   - spacing, radius, and layout rules
   - one memorable visual direction
3. Check that the choices are specific to the subject rather than generic AI defaults.
4. Build the real usable experience first. Keep hierarchy, content, and controls clear.
5. Verify desktop and mobile layouts, keyboard focus, readable contrast, reduced motion, and non-overlapping content.
6. Review a screenshot or live page and remove decoration that does not improve the task.

## Design Guidance

- Choose typography deliberately; avoid default-looking font stacks when the project allows it.
- Use CSS variables for colors and repeated visual tokens.
- Let the subject matter drive palette, imagery, texture, and composition.
- Use motion sparingly: prefer one purposeful entrance or state transition over many generic hover animations.
- Use familiar icons for icon-only controls and provide accessible labels/tooltips.
- Use stable dimensions and responsive constraints for cards, media, controls, and grids.
- Keep text concise and use plain, user-facing language.
- Treat empty and error states as actionable guidance.
- Avoid repeated rounded cards, decorative gradients, excessive labels, and one-note color palettes unless the brief calls for them.

## Review Checklist

- The first viewport communicates what the product is.
- The visual language is distinctive and consistent.
- Text fits its container at mobile and desktop widths.
- Controls have visible focus states and accessible names.
- Images have useful alt text and preserve the intended crop.
- The layout remains usable with reduced motion and keyboard navigation.
